items.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023
items.q: I’m right in the middle now of doing a record with him now... he continues to be a mentor this guy... we’ve got two great musicians... Tisziji and myself... that’s how this album was done.

ctx.x: I’ve got time if you do.

Have to do a commercial? All right well ‘cause this is where the moment where I realized something had to change. First of all I didn’t really go home for the summer after my first year at the University of Toronto because there was music happening in Toronto. I just had to stay. And I told my parents, of course I visited them at the beginning and the end of the summer but in the middle I said I would like to stay in Toronto and take a course in arranging. It was really that Blood, Sweat & Tears influence hipping…

into a bunch of open-minded musicians there, all of them in the Army, and he became a guitarist of this type that I’d never seen before or since really because he doesn’t play any chords or harmonies or anything, he treats his guitar as if it were a saxophone and he were John Coltrane. And I’m still playing with him today because he and I have both — you know I came to the U.S., he returned to the U.S. after some time in Toronto and we hooked up again here and I’m right in the middle now of doing a record with…
